title: The Narada Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa and compiled over several centuries, with a second part that is largely a manual of Vaishnava devotion, law and pilgrimage.
description: The Narada Purana opens with the sages questioning Sanatkumara and turns into a wide survey of Vaishnava teaching: the greatness of Vishnu and his devotees, cosmology and the ages, the duties of the four stages of life, the rites owed to the dead, the sacred places of pilgrimage, gifts and vows, and the practice of repeating the divine name.
historicalContext: It is one of the Puranas most concerned with practice rather than story, and it preserves in passing a good deal of the religious life of medieval north India: ritual law, the tirthas, and the vratas by which ordinary worshippers lived.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of both parts as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
